prompt:
Output exactly two lines only.

Line 1 (tags) — required format and rules:
- Provide 2–5 comma-separated tokens (no punctuation except commas). Prefer exactly 3 tags when visually possible: main noun first, then 1–2 highly discriminative co-objects. You may append a visually certain count immediately after the main noun (digit or word), e.g., "child", "child 2", "person one".
- Tokens must be lower-case common nouns or single-word simple adjectives used only as visible attributes (dog, child, car, red, small). Multiword object phrases that denote a single visual object are allowed as a single token if visually fused (e.g., "wine bottle" or "traffic light").
- At least 2 tokens must be nouns (including the main noun). At most 1 token may be a visible attribute (color/size). Do NOT include verbs, proper nouns, brand names, inferred facts, emotions, events, or dates.
- Avoid generic person terms ("person","people","man","woman") when a more specific, visually plausible noun is available (prefer "child", "bicyclist", "trumpet", "wine bottle"). Deduplicate; no repeated words or near-synonyms.
- Order tags by salience (most discriminative first). Prefer compact, high-information nouns (2–4 tokens ideal).

Line 2 (caption) — required format and hard rules:
- Either (A) one factual short sentence in present simple or present progressive of 7–14 words, OR (B) a 2–3 word fallback caption (main noun + short visible location, e.g., "child sidewalk") if a compliant 7–14 word caption would require guessing. If tags cannot be produced reliably, Line 2 must be exactly "image unclear".
- The main noun from Line 1 must appear verbatim in token positions 1–3 of Line 2 (hard requirement). If Line 1 includes a numeric count, reflect it in the caption with correct morphology: singular -> third-person singular verb (adds -s), plural -> base verb and plural noun form (e.g., "1 child stands", "2 children stand").
- Include at most one clearly visible color or size and at most one simple spatial relation/preposition (on, in, near, by, in front of, behind). Use only concrete, directly visible facts. Do NOT add proper nouns, intentions, emotions, or invented facts.
- No punctuation except an optional single period at the end of the sentence.

Lexical reinforcement and anti-hallucination (HARD CONSTRAINTS):
- Require at least 2 exact token overlaps between Line 1 and Line 2 (nouns or attributes). This overlap requirement must be satisfied during candidate construction for every non-fallback candidate; do not rely on post-hoc fixes. If two reliable overlaps cannot be produced, output the 2–3 word fallback (main noun + visible location) or, if tags cannot be trusted, output "image unclear".
- If an attribute appears in tags, it must appear verbatim in the caption. Never add an attribute in the caption that is not present in tags.
- Only include a color/size when visually certain. If attribute inclusion is based on detector/segmentation output, require confidence >60% of object pixels or top detection confidence; otherwise omit the attribute.
- Forbidden: proper nouns, inferred facts, emotions, dates, brand names; no punctuation except allowed commas in Line 1 and optional final period in Line 2.

Candidate generation, systematic variation, and reranking (required):
- Internally generate N = 6 diverse compliant candidates before returning output. Force at least two exact overlaps when constructing each non-fallback candidate. If a candidate cannot meet overlap requirements without guessing, produce the fallback candidate instead.
- Controlled candidate templates (use deterministic templates and prefer detector-proposed nouns when available):
  1) main noun + most discriminative co-object (high overlap) -> "[main noun] [verb] [preposition] [co-object]" or "[main noun] with [co-object] on [location]".
  2) main noun + visible attribute (if confident) -> "[main noun] [verb] [attribute] [co-object]".
  3) main noun + spatial relation + salient object -> "[main noun] [verb] [preposition] [object]".
  4) count-aware variant if numeric count visible -> "[count] [main-noun plural] [verb] [preposition] [object]".
  5) compact 2–3 word fallback -> "[main noun] [location]".
  6) alternate high-overlap specific noun choice or adjacency variant -> "[main noun][co-object adjacent phrase] [verb] [preposition] [object]".
- Ensure at least two exact token overlaps (nouns or attribute tokens) are included in each constructed non-fallback candidate. Use adjacency (main noun next to co-object) when possible because phrase matches improve CLIP alignment.

Proxy scoring & reranking:
- If a CLIP scorer is available: normalize CLIP scores (min-max or z-score across candidates) and normalized proxy scores, then compute final_score = 0.9 * normalized_CLIP + 0.1 * normalized_proxy. Select the top candidate that passes self-checks.
- If CLIP unavailable: compute proxy_score for each candidate with updated weights to better mimic CLIP sensitivity:
  proxy_score = 10*(main-noun overlap: 1 if main noun verbatim appears in caption else 0)
               + 8*(each additional exact overlap)
               + 5*(visible-attribute overlap present)
               + positional_bonus (+3 if main noun at position 1, +1 if at position 2–3)
               - 8*(generic-noun penalty if any tag ∈ {person, people, man, woman} used when a more specific noun is reliably visible)
               - 3*(duplicates-collapsed penalty)
               - 4*(each tag beyond 3)
               - 1*(each caption word beyond 12)
- Normalize proxy_score across candidates (min-max or z-score) before combining or selecting top candidate. Break ties by: more exact overlaps, fewer tags, main noun at position 1.

Deterministic self-checks (must pass before returning output):
1. Tags: 2–5 comma-separated tokens, all lower-case nouns/adjectives only, ≤1 attribute, deduplicated.
2. Caption: 7–14 words OR valid 2–3 word fallback OR exactly "image unclear".
3. Overlap: ≥2 exact token overlaps between Line 1 and Line 2. If not met, candidate invalid.
4. Main noun position: main noun verbatim appears at token position 1–3 in the caption.
5. Count/morphology: if Line 1 has a numeric count, caption morphology must match (pluralization and verb form).
6. Attribute mirroring: if an attribute appears in tags, the same token must appear verbatim in the caption.
7. Forbidden content: no proper nouns, inferred facts, emotions; no punctuation except allowed commas in Line 1 and optional final period in Line 2.

Fallback and conservatism:
- If fewer than 2 high-confidence nouns can be produced, use the compact 2–3 word fallback (main noun + visible location) or output Line 2 = "image unclear". Be conservative: prefer "image unclear" over inventing low-confidence specifics.
- If no candidate passes self-checks after reranking, output the most reliable tags possible (2–5 tokens) on Line 1 and Line 2 = "image unclear".

Operational heuristics (optional but recommended):
- When available, use a fast object detector/segmenter to propose high-confidence nouns and attributes; prioritize those proposals when building tags and candidates.
- If CLIP is available, run light lexical search (synonym/plural/attribute inclusion variants) scored by CLIP to pick the top valid candidate.
- Log cases with large negative delta_clip for later analysis and iterative tuning of generic-noun penalties and attribute confidence thresholds.

Output requirement reminder:
- The VLM must follow the two-line output format exactly: Line 1 = tags (2–5 comma-separated tokens, prefer 3), Line 2 = caption (7–14 words) OR 2–3 word fallback OR "image unclear". No extra lines or commentary.
